item_01.why_target: Each set lies in one part, so parts colour independently and discrepancy is the larger.
item_01.why_bound: sqrt(n log(m/n)) squares to n log(m/n), which adds side by side.

item_02.why_target: Size cost accumulates linearly in the number of amplification steps.
item_02.why_bound: k-fold repetition raises size to the k-th power.

item_03.why_target: CFGS value is ceil(n^{1/2}) and n is additive, so squares add.
item_03.why_bound: log(n1+n2) equals max(log n1, log n2) up to an additive constant, so the bound refuses to accumulate.

item_04.why_target: Product of caps is a cap of size |A1|*|A2|.
item_04.why_bound: 3^n times a polynomial saving that does not tensor.

item_05.why_target: (1-eps^2)^{O(k)} decays as a constant to the power k.

item_06.why_bound: The conjectured invariant is exactly the multiplicative law.

item_07.why_target: Merging hard point sets forces dimensions to add; log n is additive.
item_07.why_bound: O(log n / eps^2) is linear in the additive quantity log n.

item_08.why_target: alpha(C5 box C5) = 5 strictly exceeds alpha(C5)^2 = 4, so the quantity beats multiplicativity; hence the limit definition.

item_09.why_target: Largest root of a direct sum is the largest among blocks; flat in block count.
item_09.why_bound: tr exp sums every block's contribution, so the bound accumulates additively.

item_10.why_target: Tensor of a product instance is the tensor product.
item_10.why_bound: Border rank is submultiplicative under tensor product.

item_11.why_target: CFGS ceil(n^{1/2}) with n additive, so squares add.
item_11.why_bound: A1 (x) I + I (x) A2 squares to (n1+n2)I, so sqrt(n) obeys the l2 law.

item_12.why_target: Product of downward-closed extremal systems has |S1|*|S2| sets.
item_12.why_bound: Sauer-Shelah behaves like n^d with d additive.

item_13.why_target: 367 in C7^{box 5} strictly beats alpha(C7)^5 = 243, so supermultiplicative, no law of these shapes.

item_14.why_target: Combining hard range spaces of VC dim d1 and d2 gives one of dim d1+d2 whose requirement is the sum.
item_14.why_bound: O((d/eps)log(1/eps)) is linear in d, which is additive.
